title: Cash transfers raise women’s employment when public services are better
summary: In Brazil, a large unconditional cash transfer made mothers of young children more likely to find formal work by helping them send their children to school, with the biggest gains where local education services were better funded.

title: Can forest management plans make industrial logging more sustainable?
summary: Evidence from logging concessions across five Congo Basin countries shows that forest management plan validation reduces annual forest loss by nearly half. The benefits emerge gradually, underscoring the importance of timely implementation and long-term evaluation.

title: This week in development economics at VoxDev: 06/11/2026
summary: This week we featured research on supply chains, economic inclusion, manufacturing and more!

title: Can a low-cost career guidance workshop keep teenagers in school?
summary: A half-day career guidance workshop, built around a personalised app, raised high school enrolment and completion in rural Cambodia. Gains lasted more than three years after the intervention.

title: Can service-led growth replace factory-led development?
summary: Many of today’s fastest-growing developing economies, from India to Kenya, have bypassed industrialisation, with workers moving straight from farms into non-tradable consumer services. New structural estimates suggest that productivity growth in these services has genuinely driv…

title: Can economic inclusion reduce prejudice against disability?
summary: In Uganda, a disability-inclusive anti-poverty programme helped people with disabilities move from insecure casual work into farming, but it did not reduce prejudice against them, and on one measure prejudice rose.

title: The state of international development
summary: Rohini Pande joined us to discuss the state of international development, based on the introductory chapter of the Handbook of Development Economics, Volume 6, on which she is a co-editor.

title: What makes supply chains resilient? Evidence from India's COVID-19 lockdowns
summary: Supply chains built on complex inputs and large, well-connected suppliers held up through India's 2020 COVID-19 lockdowns. Firms buying easily replaced inputs were far quicker to cut supplier links.

title: Why democracy alone does not build effective states
summary: Building an effective state that raises broad-based taxes, enforces the law, and provides health and education is a political problem as much as a technocratic one. Data from 1990 and 2016 points to three persistent clusters of states, but history is not destiny: executive const…

title: How returning Indigenous land empowers communities without guaranteeing environmental benefits
summary: In Chile, returning ancestral land to Mapuche communities led them to replace commercial pine and eucalyptus plantations with grasslands for livestock, but it brought no measurable gains in carbon storage or biodiversity.

title: Why do so many people in poor countries work in small firms?
summary: In India, most manufacturing workers are in small firms partly because most customers can only afford cheap, low-quality goods that small workshops make efficiently, and this explains up to around 40% of the gap in firm size between India’s poorer and richer states.

title: This week in development economics at VoxDev: 30/10/2026
summary: This week we featured research on sanctions, progressive taxation, pension reform and more!

title: Fewer barrels, dirtier barrels: The hidden environmental cost of US sanctions on Venezuela’s oil
summary: After US sanctions, Venezuela flared more than twice as much gas for each barrel of oil it produced, as shortages of imported diluent overloaded its oil infrastructure.

title: How pension cuts push households to save more and work longer
summary: In urban China, cuts to pension generosity in 1997 and 2005 led households to save more and work longer, explaining around a quarter of the rise in the household saving rate and half the rise in working hours between 1995 and 2009.

title: Do women underreport domestic violence to male enumerators?
summary: Women in Bangladesh reported more intimate partner violence to female survey enumerators than their male counterparts, changing impact estimates of BRAC’s Ultra-Poor Graduation programme.

title: Armed groups as states: Taxation, security, and civilian support

title: How does progressive taxation shape revenue and incidence in low-capacity states?
